Keep the frozen area-balanced global two-way decoder from the selected parent unchanged.

Parent random-walk objective plus a timing-weighted star-edge
consistency term on the supplied graph dot products. Each star edge is
weighted by its frozen per-edge timing share (weights of one net sum to
its full net weight), so nets with a large delay/slack spread dominate
the attraction and their endpoint groups are pulled into the same
embedding region, which the unchanged two-way decoder then keeps on one
die. Expected measurable effect: lower timing-weighted cut and lower
final WNS/TNS violation deficit at identical area-closure behaviour.
The term is a weight-normalized average (finite and zero when the graph
has no edges) and is ramped in with epoch progress so early epochs keep
the parent scoring geometry.

Unchanged parent decoder: the frozen area-balanced global two-way
clustering, so any timing delta is attributable to the loss geometry.

model_docstrings.docstring:
Parent optimized only random-walk positive/negative pairs.

Change relative to parent: add a normalized timing-weighted graph-star
attraction term over the supplied represented-net edges. Since
graph_scores are embedding dot products, (1 - graph_scores) is half the
squared Euclidean distance between L2-normalized endpoints. Weighting it
by graph_weights biases the embedding geometry toward keeping endpoints
of high timing-weight nets close, so the area-balanced two-means decoder
is more likely to place them on the same die.

Expected measurable effect: lower timing-weighted cross-die cut and
improved WNS/TNS versus the parent, especially on seeds where the parent
cuts high-weight nets.

Invalidating result: unchanged final labels/cut or worse mean timing
across cases and seeds would reject this graph-attraction hypothesis.

Unchanged from parent.

This loss_only candidate tests only the loss-induced embedding geometry.
The decoder remains the frozen seeded area-balanced weighted two-way
clustering helper, so any timing change must come from the loss rather
than decoder behavior.

model_docstrings.docstring:
Unchanged maintained negative-sampling objective.

This is a decoder-only experiment, so the embedding loss keeps its exact
parent behaviour (plain random-walk positive/negative logistic loss). The
expected measurable effect is zero change attributable to the loss; any
WNS/TNS movement is attributable to the handoff split below.

Balanced Lloyd split of the learned embeddings (replaces reference k-means).

The reference helper optimises unconstrained area-weighted two-means and
leaves the topology balance to the protected closure. Here the split
direction is the difference of physical-area-weighted group centres and
every step re-thresholds at the area-weighted quantile of the projected
embeddings, so the returned labels already sit on the 0.5 area target and
use exactly the area-weighted centres the protected squared-distance
margin recomputes. Expected effect: fewer native closure moves and a
lower timing-weighted cut, i.e. less negative WNS/TNS versus the parent.

model_docstrings.docstring: Reproduce the maintained random-walk negative-sampling objective.

Area-balanced cosine reassignment of the frozen two-means labels.

Parent returned the seeded area-balanced weighted two-means labels directly.
This candidate keeps that single unchanged helper call for the two centers,
then reassigns all groups by area-balanced ranking of the cosine-similarity
difference between the two physical-area-weighted centers. Expected effect:
assignments follow the L2-normalized dot-product geometry used by the loss,
which can sharpen the learned communities and improve post-flow timing.
Invalidation: if the decoded labels are rejected, final cut/timing does not
improve versus the parent, or the paired physical score regresses.
